utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Since we had a surgeon in our room, an exceptional expert, (redacted), he said that it was the man's stomach. He kept complaining about his stomach, actually pointing at his stomach. And even before (redacted) could examine him, he realised that the pain was in his stomach and that he had to have surgery performed on him so they could see what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was surgery ever performed on him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. No. Regrettably not. He passed away. One morning -- I mean, I said that these rooms consist of two or three rooms, and he was in another room where people slept. It's the same room but this is a different part of that room. And they told us that Kunovac had died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the doctor told the guard that Mr. Kunovac needed surgery?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: The doctor went to see this physician of ours, this male nurse, this medical technician, Jokanovic, who was in charge of us, and he gave him some kind of tablets. He brought him these tablets, but, regrettably, he did not manage to survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone else dying at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before you go on, Ms. Kuo, perhaps it's only the second time that we've heard that story, but there was no issue taken with it at all, as I understand. We don't want to have the same story told by every witness unless there is some real need to add to the story or there has been some suggestion that it wasn't true. But it's up to the accused to take issue with it if it's going to be in issue. Nobody took issue with the doctor about that particular evidence, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. We -- as you mentioned, this is the second time, and we are not completely sure how much we need to reinforce it, but if the Court tells us that once is enough, then that's how we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm happy to let you have the second time, but I thought I should remind you that we said at the very beginning that we don't want to hear this from every witness. There will be some cases, obviously, where you will have to produce some supporting evidence, but in that case, as I recall, there was no cross-examination about it at all and we had a very detailed piece of evidence from the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll take that into consideration. We're mindful of the weight to be given evidence if it's corroborated and so forth, so that's why we're doing that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But do you need to corroborate evidence where on the face of it it is a straightforward story and it has not been challenged? That's the point I'm making.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. That's a point well taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember any other person dying at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. Not in my room. Sandal died in this other room, Sandal, an elderly man. He was probably 75. He managed to escape, and they found him in Pljevlja and returned him to Foca. He was in the police station in Pljevlja for about ten days. They beat him there. He told us the story. He said it was terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he die?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: He died -- he died in the room where he slept also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of what cause?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone else who died?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. I remember a driver who died two days before me [as interpreted]. His name was Esad Hodzic. They told me about this. He had a job as a driver in the automobile association.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he die of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: He had had an ulcer. He felt sick in the evening. The other guys asked the guards to take him to hospital. They didn't want to. They said, "Let him wait until the morning."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning he was dead?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. I think that in the morning when he was so exhausted he was taken to hospital but it was too late by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone else who died?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I remember -- I can't remember his name now. This was this one man who hanged himself in a solitary confinement cell. Juso Dzamalija was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know why he hanged himself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there detainees who were taken away and never returned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of their names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Well, there are quite a few names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you tell us the ones you remember.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: May I look into my notes to have them remind me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have notes -- are you able to give the names without looking at your notes or not?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Ismet Pasovic; Hajro Sabanovic; Saban Durak; Emin Nesbir and his brother; Tulek, the two Tulek brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their first names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Their last name was Tulek. One worked as a policeman in the KP Dom before that and the other one worked in Maglic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember their names, their first names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: The name of one of them is Kemal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: That is C-25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Dzemal Palic, Murat Crneta, Hasan Dzano, Aziz Hasikovic, Halim Seljanci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these people taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: They were taken for an exchange. They were picked up and taken for an exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if they were actually exchanged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know. Dr. Torlak from my room went for an exchange. Then also from that room (redacted) as well, he went to be exchanged. Dr. Berberkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why don't we do it this way? Perhaps we can have the usher show the witness P55, Schedule C, and we can go through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what I'd like for you to do is go through this list of names, and only for the names where you know, where you know the person, what happened to the person at KP Dom, tell us about it. So just start at the top, and then as you go through it, stop and tell us what you know.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Number one, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Only the ones that you know what happened.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Juso Dzamalija is the one I said hanged himself. Dzelilovic Kemal, he was a teacher at the school centre. Dzendusic Ramo, he was a clerk in the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you. When you said Dzelilovic Kemal, did you see him at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know [Realtime transcript read in error "I know"].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dzendusic Ramo, did you see him --

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that the previous answer was I "don't know" because the transcript says "I know."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Hodzic Nail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: They took him out in the evening. They took him out of the room where he slept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I have no idea. He was taken to the gate, and what happened to him, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him taken to the gate?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivancic Mate, do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kiselica Esad you've already told us.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, the number four I told you about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And continuing down the list, who was the next person that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Konjo Halim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I know that he was at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Krajcin Adil?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Krajcin Adil was a manager for commercial affairs at the mine. I know him very well. He was taken out one afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: To the gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know. They told us that he was going to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue down the list, please, and tell us who you know.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Kuloglija, I don't know. Mandzo I don't know. Marinovic Krunoslav, I don't know him. I think he was some kind of a journalist. I don't know whether it's him, actually. I don't know. Mujezinovic, I don't know. Nisic Nurko, I told you about him. That was that policeman, the deputy commander. He was retired, though, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rikalo Husein you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Ramovic -- yes, I told you about the Rikalos. Husein is the one who had a nickname, Husko. Everybody called him Husko. Husein is his real name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, I interrupted you, did you know Mr. Ramovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise any other names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Kemal Tulek was the policeman I told you about who had worked at the KP Dom before. And his brother, the one I told you about, I can't remember his first name, I found him in the solitary confinement cell when I was there for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You found Kemal Tulek, or his brother?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No, his brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recognise any other names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I know Munib Veiz and Veiz, Zulfo. This one was the manager of a vegetable store, Munib Veiz. His father was in the same room with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Munib Veiz?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Munib was also taken out, and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said his father was in the same room with you. What was his father's name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, his father arrived in August. He had already left the camp, his son. His father's name is Edhem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Edhem Veiz ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I heard that he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him injured?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Zulfo Veiz?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Zulfo Veiz was also there. I heard that he was beaten as well, but I don't know what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: This exhibit is no longer necessary for this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the warden of KP Dom was during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: At the time that I was there, Milorad Krnojelac, called Mico, everybody called him Mico, was the warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Krnojelac from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We would meet almost every day. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said you would meet, were you on friendly terms, on social terms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: We would greet each other. We didn't socialise, but we would always greet one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that Milorad Krnojelac was the warden of KP Dom at this time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Everybody called him "warden," from the police officers, the cooks. And if we had to complain or make a request, then we would have to announce ourselves for him to see us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever request to see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Well, I thought about it several times, but I didn't have the courage to request it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krnojelac at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Perhaps once a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this during the daytime or at nighttime?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: During the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you see him doing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: He would usually walk through the yard or the complex, so we would meet sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said, "We would meet sometimes," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Well, in the complex, I would see him; also from the window of our room, because our windows looked directly onto the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he wearing when you would see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: He always had a military dress on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say military dress, can you describe it more specifically? Was it the olive-green uniform? Was it camouflage? What kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: It was the plain one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The olive-green, you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. The uniforms, the light ones that the, that the army used to wear before. The olive-grey was the winter uniform. This was the summer uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if -- seeing him with a firearm, or not?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, I wasn't able to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Milorad Krnojelac in KP Dom, was he alone or with other people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I would often see him alone. Sometimes I would see him with the cooks. So he would be in the company of his people from the furniture factory, the craftsmen, so usually this would be the company that I would see him in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him with other prison staff?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Which staff? Which prison staff do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, the deputy warden or the commander of guards or --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. This is a disputed question, so why not ask, for example, with the cook? Why is the question with the deputy, and so on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm at a loss to understand what your problem is. Are you saying it's a leading question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well then, if you say that, we'll hear what Ms. Kuo has got to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I tried to ask a non-leading question, Your Honour, but the witness wanted more specifics. He wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I know that, but Mr. Bakrac is nothing if not anxious to ensure there are no leading questions in this case, sometimes unreasonably so, but this time I think there is some reason to it. A very simple question would be: Did you ever see him with any senior members of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever see Milorad Krnojelac with any other senior members of his staff?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I saw him once with Petko Cancar and Vojislav Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those two people employees at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. No. Petko was the president of the municipality, and I don't know what post Maksimovic held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Maksimovic a politician?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why these two individuals were with Mr. Krnojelac in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: At that time, Foca was getting a medical faculty, so they went to the furniture factory. According to what the people who worked in the furniture factory said, there was some question of cabinets for the medical faculty, for the school of medicine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the -- in answer to an earlier question, you said that Mr. Krnojelac was sometimes with his people at the furniture factory. What did you mean by that? Who was "his people"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Well, his people who worked with our people, the craftsmen. They were probably qualified carpenters and other craftsmen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those craftsmen detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. No. These were people who previously worked at KP Dom, the craftsmen. This was called the Drina Economic Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you could tell, was there any separation between the economic unit and the rest of the KP Dom in terms of its administration or did it function as a whole unit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: If that's what you're asking me, I think that before it was one unit and it wasn't separated, and it was called an economic unit. I don't know whether during the war they separated the farm, the economic part, from the furniture factory. I don't know how this worked as a whole. But I know that before it was called Drina Economic Unit. They would produce eggs, milk. They would also then produce furniture there and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this directly: As far as you could tell, was Milorad Krnojelac the warden of the entire KP Dom or only of the economic unit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether he was the warden or he managed the economy there as well, but I know that there was an earlier warden of KP Dom at the economic part. His name was Raso.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is only the time that you were there. Was there a separation of the economic unit of which Mr. Krnojelac was warden only or was he warden of the entire KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when there was a new warden brought to KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I remember -- I think it was October when they came by. The new warden, his name was Sekulovic, who worked in the marketing at Oslobodjenje in Gorazde. He was accompanied by the former warden of KP Dom, Raso, and Mr. Krnojelac. So it was the three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that he became the new warden, Mr. Sekulovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Me and Professor Husein Lojo were working. We were sorting through the beans in front of the kitchen and that's the way they were passing on their way to the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that there was a new warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Raso came up to us. All three of them came up to us, to the table, and they talked to us. And Raso, the former warden, knew Mr. Sekulovic. He knew him like I did. He said, "This is" -- oh, he was introducing him to me. He said this is (redacted). And when we were on reserve and when it was a critical matter with oil and sugar, I gave that to the KP Dom because the reserves that we had and the regulations managing those reserves, when there is a shortage of supplies in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hospital, in the KP Dom, and also when there are some natural disasters, we would be allowed to issue these goods. I had the right to issue them. And because there was a major shortage of oil and sugar, I gave them to the KP Dom on condition that they return the same quantities of those goods to us. And this is what he said to this warden, to Sekulovic. He told him about my small contribution in the past to KP Dom, that I had given help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had given help, that was before the war, right, or was it while you were --

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sekulovic say something to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: He told Raso that he knew me. He said, "Perhaps (redacted) didn't remember me." But I remember. I went with that journalist. That journalist was a friend of mine, Radisic from Gorazde, and whenever he came to Foca he would visit me at my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told anything about being released?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes, he did say something. Sekulovic told me quietly, "You will be exchanged within 15 days." This was the happiest day for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that conversation, did Mr. Krnojelac say anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. He was with Raso, right next to the table where we were sorting through the beans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, in fact, released within 15 days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: No. A couple of days passed and I told the professor, I told him, "Nothing will come of this exchange," and we laughed. But on the third day, Milutinvic was coming from the exchange and he called me, because we were outside. We were cleaning the beans outside at the table. And he called out to me and he said, "(redacted) get ready in 10 minutes. You will be exchanged." And I laughed and I said, "It's not possible." And he said, "Yes, yes. It's true." So I got ready in ten minutes. At the gate, the police officer on duty, it's his duty to search a person. He said, "What do you have? What are you taking out of the KP Dom?" And also, it is their obligation to return to a person those things that they left there once they were brought to KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken when you were taken out of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: When I took all of my things, the police chief commander Rasevic returned my driver's licence to me, and I don't know what else. And then this police officer escorted me to another door. There was a Golf vehicle waiting outside. One person, I think his name Elez - I don't know his name, I don't know that he worked at the post office - and in new warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you where they were taking you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. They told me, "You're going to be exchanged." Elez even said to me -- he whispered. He said, "You're going to be exchanged for my son."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: To Kula, the Kula camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of camp is Kula?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: That was also an economic unit. It was some kind of prison but it belonged to the Sarajevo region. It was a part of the central prison of Sarajevo. They also had an economija, economic unit for the production of eggs, fruits, and vegetables, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was being detained at Kula camp during this time, do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: At that time, I saw (redacted) from Foca there and also another person. I can't remember his name. He had crutches. Hadzimesic, Hadzimusic Ahmo. They left Foca before I did. (redacted), I think, left on July 5th, and this person left -- the other person left on August 15th to be exchanged, this Ahmo. So I saw them in Kula. I was surprised when I found them there because when I arrived there, they told me at the entrance the warden was there. He just happened to be on the steps of the Kula camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Kula camp also being used as a detention centre at this time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. About 250 people were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the 250 people Muslims or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: One sleeping room was occupied by Serbs. The rest were Serbs and Muslims. Later, they brought women and children from Rogatica so that one of the sleeping rooms were older people, children. There was a baby as well. It was six months old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you taken from KP Dom to the Kula camp?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I left KP Dom on the 15th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the Kula camp?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I stayed seven and a half months at the Kula camp. So on the 27th of July, I was captured in Titograd, and on the 27th of July, I was exchanged. So that means that I was there for 26 months in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said you were captured in Titograd on the 27th of July; is that right? Because earlier you said May.

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: The 27th of May. I apologise, it was the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, as a result of the time that you spent in the KP Dom, what physical effects do you suffer?

utterances.speaker: FWS-162
utterances.text: I have pains in my back. I have psychological trauma. If I see any of these details in the evening, I get very upset, the mass exhumations and so on. I try to shield myself from that. I'm irritable. I use medication.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Those are all the Prosecution questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, or Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It's five to four. I don't know if the Defence should start with the cross-examination in view of the fact that we only have such a brief time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you'd prefer not to, we're happy to give you five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that we could only cover the initial questions, and that wouldn't really help us too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Mr. Bakrac also has a request for the Trial Chamber. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But we don't need the witness any more for the moment? Perhaps you better wait there for a moment, sir. It will save some time. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for now, yes. Your Honour, I apologise for the misunderstanding, but the question is not connected with the witness, so there's no need for the witness to stay. Perhaps we can release him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. We will be seeing you again early in the New Year when we resume. The Victims and Witnesses Unit will be able to explain it all to you. Thank you for your attendance. We shall see you next year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bakrac, I thought it might have been about the witness. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. I wanted to ask one question. Perhaps it's better to say, to make a request to the Trial Chamber. I understood that the trial will continue on January the 8th, 2001. So because we have the Orthodox holidays later, so the Orthodox and New Year's holidays are on the 7th of January, I wanted to make a request, if this didn't interfere too much with the Trial Chamber's schedule, if possible to resume the proceedings one week later, if this is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It seems very reasonable, Mr. Bakrac. Yes, certainly. I can assure you we will be very busy at that time trying to polish up our judgement of the preceding trial, so it's not as if we will have nothing to do. Is there any problem from the Prosecution's point of view?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we will resume, then, on the 15th, that will be, 15th of January, 2001, at 9.30, and I hope you have a very happy Orthodox Christmas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much. Thank you very much for granting my request, and I, of course, wish a happy Christmas to everybody in the courtroom and also the New Year's holidays.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, very, very briefly. The Deputy Registrar has asked us to put this on the record. We now have the full translations of a number of exhibits that were introduced by Ms. Thapa, and we would like to distribute them so they can be put in officially on the record. It is 2A, 4A, 5A, and 38A, and we have copies for everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
